ascii-art-generator.formula:
1. Draw the source (typed text or uploaded photo) onto a hidden canvas.
2. For each cell, compute the average brightness: (R + G + B) / 3.
3. Map brightness to a character with this ramp (dark to light):
   '@%#*+=-:. '
   index = floor(brightness / 255 x 10)
4. Join characters into rows of plain text.

Text mode uses 10x20 px cells; image mode halves the height first so characters (taller than wide) keep the proportions right.
howTo: Pick Text mode for a banner or Image mode to convert a photo.
In text mode, type your word (up to 40 characters). In image mode, choose an image file under 5 MB.
Move the width slider: more characters means more detail but a wider block of text.
Try the invert switch if dark areas should be light and vice versa.
Copy the art or download it as a .txt file and paste it anywhere plain text works.
keyFacts: ASCII art represents an image using only printable text characters.
Each character stands in for one block of pixels, chosen by that block's brightness.
The character ramp used here, dark to light, is: @ % # * + = - : . (space).
Dark pixels become dense characters like @; bright pixels become spaces.
Text mode draws your word in a bold monospace font, then samples it exactly like a photo.
Because characters are taller than wide, images are squashed vertically before sampling to keep shapes proportional.

ascii-art-generator.quickAnswer: ASCII art turns pictures or words into images made of text characters. Type a word to get a banner, or upload a photo (under 5 MB) to convert it. Each block of pixels is replaced by a character chosen for its brightness: dark areas become @ and %, light areas become dots and spaces. Adjust the width for more detail, flip the invert switch if needed, then copy or download the result as plain text.
ascii-art-generator.tagline: Turn text into banners and photos into retro text art.
ascii-art-generator.workedExample:
Take a tiny 2x2 image with these pixel brightness values:
Row 1: 0 (black), 85 (dark grey)
Row 2: 170 (light grey), 255 (white)

Ramp (dark to light): @ % # * + = - : . (space)
index = floor(brightness / 255 x 10)

1. Pixel 0: floor(0 / 255 x 10) = 0 -> '@'
2. Pixel 85: floor(85 / 255 x 10) = floor(3.33) = 3 -> '*'
3. Pixel 170: floor(170 / 255 x 10) = floor(6.67) = 6 -> '-'
4. Pixel 255: floor(255 / 255 x 10) = floor(10) = 10 -> capped at 9 -> ' ' (space)

Result:
@*
-  (dash followed by a space)
mistakes: Using a busy or low-contrast photo gives muddy art — high-contrast images with a clear subject convert far better.
Cranking the width too high makes the art wrap and break in chats and comments — keep it narrow for pasting anywhere.
Text-mode art looks squished because characters are taller than wide — that is normal, not a bug; design for it.
Pasting into an app with a proportional font (like WhatsApp) ruins the alignment — art only works in monospace contexts.
Expecting color or shading to survive — it is plain text, so any color information from the image is lost in conversion.
